title: The timezone that dropped the orders
kicker: World 6 · Prove It & Fix It · Boss

job.text: New domain: a daily active users tool over an event log. It has been green for weeks — but it silently drops events that land right at midnight UTC, so days near a timezone edge undercount. The check never tested a boundary timestamp, so it stayed green on a wrong number. Expose the false green, re-direct the fix at the rule (not the one day, and not by loosening the check), and add your own adversarial boundary case that passes. In your own words you would ask the AI to run the boundary case, strengthen the check, fix the rule, and prove it; here you build that ask from the checklist. Pass or fail is decided by the deterministic case runner, never by the AI reading your words.

preview.more: events.log · the check never tested a 00:00 UTC timestamp

naivePrompt: It's been green for weeks, we're done.
basePrompt: It's been green for weeks, we're done.

moves.label: Run the check on the edge day

text.plain: Run your check on the held-out day with a midnight-UTC event, not just the ordinary days.
text.tech: Execute the check against the held-out day containing a 00:00 UTC event.

moves.label: Strengthen it so it fails here

text.plain: Add what's needed so the check goes red on the undercounted day — it must account for the boundary timestamp.
text.tech: Add the boundary-inclusive clause so the check returns False on the undercounted day.

moves.label: Fix the rule, not the day

text.plain: Fix how the tool buckets timestamps for every day — don't hard-code the one edge day.
text.tech: Fix the time-bucketing rule globally; do not special-case the failing day.

moves.label: Add a passing adversarial boundary case

text.plain: Add your own boundary case — a day with an event exactly at midnight UTC — with its correct count, and show it green.
text.tech: Add an adversarial case with a 00:00 UTC event and its committed expected count; show it passing.

text.plain: It's been green for weeks, so it's fine.
text.tech: It's been green for weeks, so it's fine.

moves.label: Just make the edge day pass

text.plain: Special-case the one edge day so it reads right.
text.tech: Hard-code the edge day's count so it reads right.

moves.label: Loosen the check so it passes

text.plain: Widen the check so the undercount falls inside the allowed range.
text.tech: Relax the check tolerance so the undercount is accepted.

rules.claim: Check now fails the old wrong answer; rule fixed for every day; boundary case green; no regression.
rules.feedback: Boss cleared. You ran the check on the edge day and watched the false green turn red, fixed the time-bucketing rule for every day, added your own midnight-UTC case, and the whole set holds — with the check tighter, not looser. That is prove-it-and-fix-it end to end.
rules.lesson: Expose the false green, fix the rule at the root, and prove it with a case that could have failed.

output.source: false green exposed, rule fixed at the root, adversarial case added

rules.claim: The edge day reads right now, but another day near the boundary is off.
rules.feedback: You fixed the day, not the rule. Hard-coding the one edge day leaves every other boundary day still undercounting. Fix how the tool buckets midnight timestamps for all days.
rules.lesson: Patching one case leaves the whole class broken.

output.source: an overfit on the one edge day

rules.claim: Everything green — because the check now tolerates the undercount.
rules.feedback: You passed it by lowering the bar. Widening the check lets the undercount through instead of catching it. A boss pass needs the check tighter, not looser — fix the tool.
rules.lesson: Loosening the check hides the bug it was built to catch.

output.source: a check weakened until the wrong count fits

rules.claim: Check now goes red on the edge day — but the tool is still wrong.
rules.feedback: Half the boss. You exposed the false green and the check now fails the edge day — good. But you never fixed the rule, so the tool still drops the midnight event and the case stays red. Fix the bucketing rule at the root.
rules.lesson: Catching the false green is step one; fixing the rule is step two.

output.source: the false green exposed but the rule not yet fixed

rules.claim: Check still passes the edge day — the wrong answer.
rules.feedback: The check passed the wrong answer. You ran it on the edge day, but it never tests the boundary timestamp, so it stays green on an undercount. Strengthen it so it goes red here first.
rules.lesson: Find the dimension the check ignores before you trust the green.

output.source: the edge day run against a check that never tested a boundary

rules.claim: "It's been green for weeks, we're done."
rules.feedback: The green lied, for weeks. The tool silently drops midnight-UTC events, but the check never tested a boundary timestamp, so it stayed green. 'Trust the green' doesn't change what the check looks at. Run the edge case, strengthen the check, fix the rule, and add a boundary case that passes.
rules.lesson: A check that never saw a boundary can be silently wrong for a long time.

output.source: a check that never tested the timezone edge

hints.nudge: It's been green for weeks but it's wrong on the edge day — so the check never looked at a boundary timestamp. What is the edge day doing that the check ignores?
hints.gap: An event lands exactly at 00:00 UTC and the tool drops it, so days near the timezone edge undercount. The check only ever tested ordinary mid-day timestamps.
hints.moves: Add Run the check on the edge day, Strengthen it so it fails here, Fix the rule, not the day, and Add a passing adversarial boundary case. Skip 'trust the green', 'make the edge day pass', and 'loosen the check' — the first ignores the bug, the second overfits, the third hides it.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "it's been green for weeks" → a tool that drops midnight events, undetected.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: run the edge case, strengthen the check until it goes red, fix the bucketing rule for every day, and add your own midnight-UTC case that passes.

template.plain: This passed its check but it's wrong at [boundary case]. Show me the check and strengthen it so it FAILS this case. Then fix the underlying rule — not just this one case, and don't loosen the check. Finally add a boundary case of your own with its correct answer and show the whole set green.
template.tech: This passed the check but is wrong at [boundary]. Strengthen the check to return False here, fix the root rule (no hard-coding, no loosening), add an adversarial boundary case with a committed expected value, and run the full set to prove all green with no regression.

notes: ChatGPT: make it run the strengthened check on the boundary case and show it going red, then show every case green after the root fix.
Copilot in Excel: add the boundary condition to the check column, confirm the bad row flips to FALSE, then re-check every row after the fix.

A chat AI that can't run code: work the boundary case by hand, confirm the check now fails it, and re-run the whole set yourself. Never accept "I checked, it's green" — a false green is exactly what it looks like.
